Traditional systems of medicine, particularly Ayurveda and Siddha in the Indian subcontinent, have relied for millennia on indigenous botanical resources and empirical pharmacopeia. Unlike reductionist modern allopathy that isolates single active chemical compounds, traditional pharmacognosy utilizes whole-plant extracts or complex mineral-herbal mixtures. Practitioners argue that these multi-compound formulations operate through synergistic biochemical pathways where secondary metabolites buffer adverse side effects and enhance bioavailability. However, modernization poses significant challenges to these ancient healing arts. The erosion of oral traditions, loss of biodiversity through habitat destruction, and the commercial over-harvesting of rare medicinal flora threaten the sustainability of wild-crafted herbs. Furthermore, the lack of standardized clinical trials and rigorous quality-control protocols often invites skepticism from the mainstream biomedical community. Bridging this gap requires integrating time-tested empirical observations with modern analytical techniques such as high-performance liquid chromatography and genomic profiling. Standardization not only ensures safety and therapeutic consistency but also validates traditional claims on an international scientific platform, paving the way for a truly integrative global healthcare model.

Q. According to the passage, what is the primary distinction between traditional medicine and modern allopathy?

A) Modern allopathy exclusively uses mineral-herbal mixtures, whereas traditional medicine uses single chemical compounds.
B) Traditional medicine utilizes whole-plant extracts or complex mixtures, whereas modern allopathy isolates single active chemical compounds.
C) Traditional medicine relies on standardized clinical trials, whereas modern allopathy depends entirely on oral traditions.
D) Modern allopathy employs high-performance liquid chromatography, whereas traditional medicine rejects analytical techniques.
answer: B) Traditional medicine utilizes whole-plant extracts or complex mixtures, whereas modern allopathy isolates single active chemical compounds.

Standardization not only ensures safety and therapeutic consistency but also validates traditional claims on an international scientific platform, paving the way for a truly integrative global healthcare model.

question:

Traditional educational frameworks have long treated failure as an endpoint, a definitive metric of student inadequacy that demands remedial correction or social penalization. Yet, cognitive science and developmental psychology increasingly demonstrate that errors and setbacks are not merely incidental to learning but constitute its very bedrock. When a learner encounters cognitive dissonance—the friction between prior mental models and unexpected feedback—the brain initiates complex neurobiological reorganization. This constructive struggle forces learners to interrogate their underlying assumptions, discard flawed heuristics, and construct robust, flexible conceptual frameworks. In contrast, pristine success often reinforces surface-level memorization without demanding deep structural adaptation. Therefore, progressive classrooms must cultivate psychological safety where missteps are reframed as diagnostic data rather than moral shortcomings. By destigmatizing errors, educators empower students to take intellectual risks, explore novel problem spaces, and develop the metacognitive resilience essential for lifelong inquiry.

According to the passage, what is the primary consequence of pristine success in traditional educational settings?

A) It triggers complex neurobiological reorganization in the brain.
B) It reinforces surface-level memorization without deep structural adaptation.
C) It fosters psychological safety and encourages intellectual risk-taking.
D) It serves as definitive diagnostic data for remedial correction.
answer: B) It reinforces surface-level memorization without deep structural adaptation.
options: A) It triggers complex neurobiological reorganization in the brain.
B) It reinforces surface-level memorization without deep structural adaptation.
C) It fosters psychological safety and encourages intellectual risk-taking.
D) It serves as definitive diagnostic data for remedial correction.
explanation: The passage explicitly states that pristine success often reinforces surface-level memorization without demanding deep structural adaptation, contrasting it with the cognitive benefits of struggle and failure. Option A describes the result of failure, while options C and D describe the goals of progressive classrooms, making them incorrect.

question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Traditional educational frameworks have long treated failure as an endpoint, a definitive metric of student inadequacy that demands remedial correction or social penalization. Yet, cognitive science and developmental psychology increasingly demonstrate that errors and setbacks are not merely incidental to learning but constitute its very bedrock. When a learner encounters cognitive dissonance—the friction between prior mental models and unexpected feedback—the brain initiates complex neurobiological reorganization. This constructive struggle forces learners to interrogate their underlying assumptions, discard flawed heuristics, and construct robust, flexible conceptual frameworks. In contrast, pristine success often reinforces surface-level memorization without demanding deep structural adaptation. Therefore, progressive classrooms must cultivate psychological safety where missteps are reframed as diagnostic data rather than moral shortcomings. By destigmatizing errors, educators empower students to take intellectual risks, explore novel problem spaces, and develop the metacognitive resilience essential for lifelong inquiry.

Consider the following statements regarding the author's arguments in the passage:
(I) Errors and setbacks are fundamental components of the learning process rather than incidental occurrences.
(II) Traditional educational frameworks view failure as a positive indicator of cognitive restructuring.
(III) Progressive classrooms should foster psychological safety to treat missteps as diagnostic data.

Which of the above statements are correct according to the passage?

A) (I) and (II) only
B) (II) and (III) only
C) (I) and (III) only
D) (I), (II) and (III)
options: A) (I) and (II) only
B) (II) and (III) only
C) (I) and (III) only
D) (I), (II) and (III)
explanation: Statement (I) is correct because the passage states errors 'constitute its very bedrock'. Statement (III) is correct as the text advocates for progressive classrooms to cultivate psychological safety where missteps are diagnostic data. Statement (II) is incorrect because traditional frameworks view failure as student inadequacy, not as a positive indicator of cognitive restructuring.

गद्यांश को पढ़िए और प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

पारंपरिक शैक्षिक प्रणालियों ने लंबे समय से असफलता को एक अंत बिंदु के रूप में माना है, जो छात्र की अपर्याप्तता का एक निश्चित पैमाना है जिसके लिए उपचारात्मक सुधार या सामाजिक दंड की आवश्यकता होती है। फिर भी, संज्ञानात्मक विज्ञान और विकासात्मक मनोविज्ञान तेजी से यह प्रदर्शित करते हैं कि त्रुटियाँ और झटके सीखने की प्रक्रिया में केवल आकस्मिक नहीं हैं बल्कि इसका मुख्य आधार हैं। जब एक शिक्षार्थी को संज्ञानात्मक असंगति का सामना करना पड़ता है—पूर्व मानसिक मॉडलों और अप्रत्याशित प्रतिक्रिया के बीच घर्षण—तो मस्तिष्क जटिल न्यूरोबायोलॉजिकल पुनर्गठन शुरू करता है। यह रचनात्मक संघर्ष शिक्षार्थियों को उनकी अंत्येष्टि मान्यताओं की जांच करने, त्रुटिपूर्ण युक्तियों को त्यागने और मजबूत, लचीले वैचारिक ढांचे का निर्माण करने के लिए मजबूर करता है। इसके विपरीत, दोषरहित सफलता अक्सर गहरी संरचनात्मक अनुकूलन की मांग किए बिना सतही स्तर के स्मरण को सुदृढ़ करती है। इसलिए, प्रगतिशील कक्षाओं को मनोवैज्ञानिक सुरक्षा विकसित करनी चाहिए जहाँ गलतियों को नैतिक कमियों के बजाय नैदानिक डेटा के रूप में फिर से परिभाषित किया जाए। त्रुटियों को कलंकमुक्त करके, शिक्षक छात्रों को बौद्धिक जोखिम उठाने, नवीन समस्या क्षेत्रों का पता लगाने और आजीवन पूछताछ के लिए आवश्यक मेटाकॉग्निटिव लचीलापन विकसित करने के लिए सशक्त बनाते हैं।

गद्यांश में लेखक के तर्कों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
(I) त्रुटियाँ और झटके आकस्मिक घटनाओं के बजाय सीखने की प्रक्रिया के मूलभूत घटक हैं।
(II) पारंपरिक शैक्षिक प्रणालियाँ असफलता को संज्ञानात्मक पुनर्गठन के सकारात्मक संकेतक के रूप में देखती हैं।
(III) प्रगतिशील कक्षाओं को गलतियों को नैदानिक डेटा के रूप में मानने के लिए मनोवैज्ञानिक सुरक्षा को बढ़ावा देना चाहिए।

गद्यांश के अनुसार उपर्युक्त में से कौन से कथन सही हैं?

A) केवल (I) और (II)
B) केवल (II) और (III)
C) केवल (I) और (III)
D) (I), (II) और (III)
options_hi: A) केवल (I) और (II)
B) केवल (II) और (III)
C) केवल (I) और (III)
D) (I), (II) और (III)
explanation_hi: कथन (I) सही है क्योंकि गद्यांश बताता है कि त्रुटियाँ 'इसका मुख्य आधार हैं'। कथन (III) सही है क्योंकि पाठ प्रगतिशील कक्षाओं से मनोवैज्ञानिक सुरक्षा विकसित करने की वकालत करता है जहाँ गलतियाँ नैदानिक डेटा होती हैं। कथन (II) गलत है क्योंकि पारंपरिक प्रणालियाँ असफलता को छात्र की अपर्याप्तता मानती हैं, न कि संज्ञानात्मक पुनर्गठन के सकारात्मक संकेतक के रूप में।
